metadata.title: BioMy Research-Grade Temporal Pharmacokinetic Catalog
metadata.disclaimer: This catalog contains illustrative and peer-reviewed parameters compiled for computational research. It is not an approved clinical prescribing database. Parameters reflect healthy adult references unless renal/hepatic adjustments are explicitly applied.

drugs.name: Paracetamol
drugs.age_restrictions: Age- and weight-dependent dosing; pediatric patients require calibrated mg/kg administration.
drugs.pregnancy_restrictions: Considered acceptable at recommended short-term therapeutic doses; avoid supratherapeutic chronic use.
drugs.renal_hepatic_cautions: Caution in chronic liver disease, chronic malnutrition, and alcohol dependency where glutathione is depleted.

provenance.source_reference: Prescott LF. Paracetamol: past, present and future. Am J Ther. 2000;7(2):143-147.
provenance.population_assumptions: Adult 70kg reference with normal hepatic function
provenance.limitations: Glucuronidation/sulfation (85%) saturates in overdose, shifting flux to CYP2E1 NAPQI formation.

drugs.name: Ibuprofen
drugs.age_restrictions: Avoid unsupervised use in infants under 3 months; elderly patients have increased GI and renal toxicity risk.
drugs.pregnancy_restrictions: Contraindicated in third trimester due to risk of premature closure of ductus arteriosus and oligohydramnios.
drugs.renal_hepatic_cautions: Avoid in advanced chronic kidney disease (eGFR < 30 mL/min); reduces renal prostaglandin synthesis.

provenance.source_reference: Davies NM. Clinical pharmacokinetics of ibuprofen. Clin Pharmacokinet. 1998;34(2):101-154.
provenance.limitations: High plasma protein binding (99%) makes unbound clearance sensitive to albumin levels.

drugs.name: Warfarin
drugs.age_restrictions: Elderly patients exhibit heightened pharmacodynamic sensitivity to vitamin K epoxide reductase inhibition.
drugs.pregnancy_restrictions: Category X: teratogenic (warfarin embryopathy); contraindicated during pregnancy.
drugs.renal_hepatic_cautions: Severe hepatic dysfunction impairs clotting factor synthesis and reduces clearance.

provenance.source_reference: Holford NH. Clinical pharmacokinetics of ethanol and warfarin. Clin Pharmacokinet. 1986;11(6):483-504.
provenance.limitations: Parameters characterize potent S-enantiomer primarily cleared by CYP2C9.

drugs.name: Phenytoin
drugs.age_restrictions: Requires therapeutic drug monitoring across all age groups; altered protein binding in neonates and elderly.
drugs.pregnancy_restrictions: Fetal hydantoin syndrome risk; specialist neurologist/obstetric review required.
drugs.renal_hepatic_cautions: In uremia or hypoalbuminemia, total drug concentration misleadingly appears low while free drug is elevated.

provenance.source_reference: Richens A. Clinical pharmacokinetics of phenytoin. Clin Pharmacokinet. 1979;4(3):153-169.
provenance.population_assumptions: Adult 70kg reference with normal plasma albumin
provenance.limitations: Saturable Michaelis-Menten elimination makes concentration response highly nonlinear near Km.

drugs.name: Metformin
drugs.age_restrictions: Not recommended in elderly without contemporaneous renal function estimation.
drugs.pregnancy_restrictions: Used in gestational diabetes under clinical supervision; crosses placenta.
drugs.renal_hepatic_cautions: Strict contraindication when eGFR < 30 mL/min due to fatal lactic acidosis accumulation risk.

provenance.source_reference: Graham GG, et al. Clinical pharmacokinetics of metformin. Clin Pharmacokinet. 2011;50(2):81-98.
provenance.limitations: Zero hepatic metabolism; 100% eliminated renally via glomerular filtration and tubular secretion.

drugs.name: Amlodipine
drugs.age_restrictions: Initiate at lower dose (2.5 mg) in elderly due to reduced clearance.
drugs.pregnancy_restrictions: Limited human data; use only if benefit justifies fetal risk.
drugs.renal_hepatic_cautions: Clearance prolonged in severe hepatic impairment.

provenance.source_reference: Meredith PA, Elliott HL. Clinical pharmacokinetics of amlodipine. Clin Pharmacokinet. 1992;22(1):22-31.
provenance.limitations: Large volume of distribution and long half-life result in slow steady-state achievement (7-8 days).

drugs.name: Midazolam
drugs.age_restrictions: Lower doses required in elderly and debilitated patients.
drugs.pregnancy_restrictions: Crosses placenta; associated with neonatal CNS depression.
drugs.renal_hepatic_cautions: Substantial first-pass metabolism makes oral bioavailability sensitive to hepatic and enterocyte CYP3A4 inhibition.

provenance.source_reference: Greenblatt DJ, et al. Midazolam: clinical pharmacokinetics. Clin Pharmacokinet. 1989;16(2):80-97.
provenance.limitations: Subject to both intestinal and hepatic CYP3A first-pass clearance.

drugs.name: Atorvastatin
drugs.age_restrictions: No general pediatric approval without specialized familial hypercholesterolemia protocol.
drugs.pregnancy_restrictions: Contraindicated in pregnancy and nursing mothers; cholesterol essential for fetal development.
drugs.renal_hepatic_cautions: Contraindicated in active liver disease or unexplained persistent transaminase elevations.

provenance.source_reference: Lennernas H. Clinical pharmacokinetics of atorvastatin. Clin Pharmacokinet. 2003;42(13):1141-1160.
provenance.limitations: Low bioavailability reflects extensive intestinal and hepatic CYP3A4 extraction.

drugs.name: Digoxin
drugs.age_restrictions: High risk in elderly due to age-related eGFR decline and reduced skeletal muscle mass.
drugs.pregnancy_restrictions: Crosses placenta; requires specialized maternal-fetal monitoring.
drugs.renal_hepatic_cautions: Clearance is directly proportional to creatinine clearance; narrow therapeutic index.

provenance.source_reference: Iisalo E. Clinical pharmacokinetics of digoxin. Clin Pharmacokinet. 1977;2(1):1-16.
provenance.population_assumptions: Adult with normal renal clearance (CrCl >= 80 mL/min)
provenance.limitations: Very narrow therapeutic window (0.8 - 2.0 ng/mL); toxicity occurs at >= 2.0 ng/mL (0.002 mg/L).

drugs.name: Cyclosporine
drugs.age_restrictions: Requires strict therapeutic drug monitoring (TDM) in all age groups.
drugs.pregnancy_restrictions: Crosses placenta; associated with prematurity and low birth weight; specialist monitoring required.
drugs.renal_hepatic_cautions: Dose-dependent nephrotoxicity is primary dose-limiting toxicity; adjust in renal impairment.

provenance.source_reference: Ptachcinski RJ, et al. Clinical pharmacokinetics of cyclosporine. Clin Pharmacokinet. 1986;11(2):107-132.
provenance.limitations: Extensive erythrocyte partitioning (blood-to-plasma ratio ~2:1); plasma TDM requires consistent temperature protocol.

drugs.name: Diltiazem
drugs.age_restrictions: Titrate cautiously in elderly patients prone to bradycardia and conduction abnormalities.
drugs.pregnancy_restrictions: Category C; teratogenic in animal models at high doses; avoid unless benefit clearly outweighs risk.
drugs.renal_hepatic_cautions: Extensive hepatic first-pass metabolism; reduce dose in severe liver cirrhosis.

provenance.source_reference: Hermann P, et al. Clinical pharmacokinetics of diltiazem. Clin Pharmacokinet. 1983;8(5):455-467.
provenance.population_assumptions: Adult with supraventricular tachycardia or essential hypertension
provenance.limitations: Nonlinear accumulation observed with chronic high-dose therapy due to saturable hepatic first-pass.

drugs.name: Nadolol
drugs.age_restrictions: Adjust dosage in elderly patients with reduced glomerular filtration rates.
drugs.pregnancy_restrictions: Crosses placenta; may produce neonatal bradycardia and hypoglycemia.
drugs.renal_hepatic_cautions: Major dependence on renal elimination; dose interval must be extended as GFR declines.

provenance.source_reference: Duchin KL, et al. Pharmacokinetics of nadolol. Am Heart J. 1984;108(4):1084-1089.
provenance.limitations: Intestinal absorption is mediated by OATP1A2 uptake and inhibited by fruit juices and tea catechins.

drugs.name: Thyroid hormone
drugs.age_restrictions: Initiate lower dose (12.5-25 mcg/day) in elderly patients with coronary disease.
drugs.pregnancy_restrictions: Thyroid hormone requirement frequently increases during pregnancy; monitor TSH closely.
drugs.renal_hepatic_cautions: Metabolism modified in thyroid storm or myxedema coma; requires slow titration.

provenance.source_reference: Colucci P, et al. A review of the pharmacokinetics of levothyroxine. Am J Ther. 2013;20(5):543-550.
provenance.population_assumptions: Hypothyroid adult reference, empty stomach administration
provenance.limitations: Extreme protein binding (>99.97% to TBG/transthyretin/albumin); circulating half-life ~7 days.

herbs.name: Piperine
herbs.age_restrictions: Supervised use only; bioenhancer increases systemic exposure of co-administered drugs.
herbs.pregnancy_restrictions: High doses may have abortifacient and uterine stimulating effects; avoid concentrated extracts.
side_effects: uncontrolled bioavailability elevation of prescription medicines

provenance.source_reference: Volak LP, et al. In vitro and human in vivo evaluation of piperine-mediated drug interactions. Drug Metab Dispos. 2008;36(8):1594-1605.
provenance.limitations: Culinary black pepper (~5% piperine) yields lower systemic exposure than concentrated bioenhancers.

herbs.name: Ashwagandha
herbs.age_restrictions: Caution in pediatric patients and elderly with thyroid disorders.
herbs.pregnancy_restrictions: Spasmolytic and abortifacient potential in animal studies; avoid during pregnancy.

provenance.source_reference: Savai J, et al. Investigation of CYP interaction potential of Withania somnifera. J Ethnopharmacol. 2015;165:102-108.
provenance.limitations: In vitro inhibition is moderate; clinical relevance depends on withanolide content of commercial brand.

herbs.name: Curcumin
herbs.age_restrictions: General caution with biliary obstruction or gallstones.
herbs.pregnancy_restrictions: Avoid medicinal extract doses during pregnancy; dietary turmeric acceptable.

provenance.source_reference: Zhang W, et al. Inhibitory effects of curcumin on human liver cytochrome P450 enzymes. Toxicol Lett. 2007;172(3):148-154.
provenance.limitations: Low aqueous solubility and rapid glucuronidation limit systemic free curcumin unless formulated with bioenhancers.

herbs.name: Ginger
herbs.age_restrictions: Safe in culinary amounts; caution with concentrated supplements in bleeding disorders.
herbs.pregnancy_restrictions: Commonly used for morning sickness (up to 1000 mg/day); higher doses require clinical review.

provenance.source_reference: Kimura I, et al. Inhibitory effects of ginger constituents on human cytochrome P450 enzymes. Biol Pharm Bull. 2010;33(5):817-822.
provenance.limitations: Mild inhibition; clinical drug interaction risk low at dietary intake levels.

herbs.name: Garlic
herbs.age_restrictions: General culinary safety; supplements require discontinuation 7-10 days before surgery.
herbs.pregnancy_restrictions: Dietary amounts safe; therapeutic supplement doses may increase bleeding.

provenance.source_reference: Foster BC, et al. Effect of garlic constituents on human cytochrome P450 2E1, 2C9, and 3A4. J Pharm Pharm Sci. 2001;4(2):176-184.
provenance.limitations: Allicin degrades rapidly in stomach acid; enteric-coated preparations alter systemic delivery.

herbs.name: Giloy
herbs.age_restrictions: Caution in patients with pre-existing autoimmune diseases due to immunostimulatory properties.
herbs.pregnancy_restrictions: Insufficient safety data; avoid medicinal extract doses during pregnancy and lactation.

provenance.source_reference: Sharma A, et al. Pharmacokinetic and CYP interaction profile of Tinospora cordifolia. J Ethnopharmacol. 2014;158:43-51.
provenance.limitations: Commercial preparations vary widely in extraction method and diterpene lactone content.

herbs.name: Berberine
herbs.age_restrictions: Contraindicated in neonates due to risk of kernicterus (displaces bilirubin from albumin).
herbs.pregnancy_restrictions: Contraindicated in pregnancy; may cause uterine contractions and fetal bilirubin displacement.

provenance.source_reference: Spinozzi S, et al. Berberine pharmacokinetics and transporter-mediated drug interactions. Clin Pharmacokinet. 2014;53(7):601-615.
provenance.population_assumptions: Adult with metabolic syndrome or type 2 diabetes
provenance.limitations: Very low oral bioavailability (~5%) due to P-gp mediated intestinal efflux; high gut lumen concentration.

herbs.name: Guggul
herbs.age_restrictions: Caution with concurrent thyroid hormone or lipid-lowering regimens.

provenance.source_reference: Cui J, et al. The guggulsterone derivative modulates nuclear receptors and CYP3A expression. Science. 2002;296(5576):2159-2162.
provenance.limitations: Guggulsterones act as both competitive CYP inhibitors in vitro and PXR transcriptional inducers in vivo.

herbs.name: Grapefruit
herbs.age_restrictions: Potent interaction risk in elderly taking calcium channel blockers or statins.
herbs.pregnancy_restrictions: Dietary intake acceptable; concentrated supplement extracts require review.

provenance.source_reference: Paine MF, et al. Furanocoumarins in grapefruit juice are mechanism-based inhibitors of CYP3A4. Drug Metab Dispos. 2006;34(5):817-825.
provenance.limitations: Intestinal enterocyte CYP3A4 inactivation exceeds hepatic effect due to minimal systemic furanocoumarin bioavailability.

herbs.name: St. John's wort
herbs.age_restrictions: High risk of Serotonin Syndrome when combined with SSRIs/SNRIs in all age groups.
herbs.pregnancy_restrictions: May affect fetal growth and uterine contractility; avoid during pregnancy.

provenance.source_reference: Markowitz JS, et al. Effect of St Johns wort on drug metabolism. JAMA. 2003;290(11):1500-1504.
provenance.population_assumptions: Adult with depressive symptoms, oral administration
provenance.limitations: Hyperforin acutely inhibits CYPs in vitro but chronically acts as a potent PXR inducer, dropping oral substrate AUC.

herbs.name: Green tea
herbs.age_restrictions: Concentrated green tea extract capsules associated with rare idiosyncratic hepatotoxicity.
herbs.pregnancy_restrictions: EGCG impairs maternal folate absorption; avoid concentrated extracts in first trimester.
side_effects: idiosyncratic transaminase elevation at high doses

provenance.source_reference: Misaka S, et al. Green tea ingestion greatly reduces systemic nadolol exposure through OATP1A2 inhibition. Clin Pharmacol Ther. 2014;95(4):432-438.
provenance.limitations: Primary clinical interaction is intestinal OATP1A2 uptake inhibition, reducing nadolol/fexofenadine bioavailability by 85%.

herbs.name: Ginseng
herbs.age_restrictions: Caution in hypertensive patients; may cause mild blood pressure elevation.
herbs.pregnancy_restrictions: Safety in pregnancy unestablished; traditional contraindication during early pregnancy.

provenance.source_reference: Hao M, et al. Effect of Panax ginseng on CYP450 enzyme activity. Drug Metab Dispos. 2008;36(8):1538-1542.
provenance.limitations: Diverse ginsenoside profiles between Asian and American ginseng yield variable clinical CYP modulation.
